tip_ats_knockouts.short: ATS software rarely auto-rejects on keywords. Knockout questions (degree, years, location) do.
tip_ats_knockouts.more: Answer knockout questions truthfully and apply where you meet them, or get a referral so a human reads your CV.

tip_keywords_honest.short: Use the posting's real terms for skills you actually have. Recruiters search for them.
tip_keywords_honest.more: Don't paste the whole posting into your CV; mirror the terms that honestly describe your work.
tip_keywords_honest.triggers: none in the MVP (was the CV screen)

tip_quantify_impact.short: Use numbers: 'raised test coverage from 41% to 58%' beats 'worked on testing'.
tip_quantify_impact.more: Action verb + what you did + a measurable result. Put your strongest line first.

tip_projects_count.short: Projects, TA work and freelance count as experience. Describe them honestly and concretely.
tip_projects_count.more: Say what you built, for whom, and what happened. 'Capstone team of 4, shipped' is honest and strong.
tip_projects_count.triggers: night after a Tailor & Apply, when the honest CV fails 1+ years

tip_tailor_over_spray.short: A tailored application to a job you really fit is much more likely to get a reply than a one-click one.
tip_tailor_over_spray.more: Tailor your summary and top bullets to each posting you really match.

tip_referrals.short: A referral gets a human to read your CV. Ask people who actually know your work.
tip_referrals.more: Make it easy for them: send a two-line blurb and the job link.

tip_informational_chats.short: Network with curiosity: ask engineers for 15 minutes of advice, not for a job.
tip_informational_chats.more: Referrals often follow real conversations. It works best before you need it.

tip_ghost_jobs.short: Postings open for months or reposted constantly may not be hiring. Prefer fresh ones.
tip_ghost_jobs.more: Check the company's own careers page and the posting date before investing effort.

tip_research_company.short: Research the company before interviews: news, product, reviews. It improves every answer.
tip_research_company.more: It also helps you judge them: layoffs, funding and reviews tell you what you're walking into.
tip_research_company.triggers: committee loss, rejection without research, eq_why_us

tip_rejection_numbers.short: In a tight market, many rejections are normal. Track applications and keep going.
tip_rejection_numbers.more: A simple spreadsheet (date, role, contact, stage) shows what's working. It's volume plus targeting.

tip_rest.short: Rest before interviews. Tired answers go worse. Schedule the search like a job.
tip_rest.more: A job search is a marathon. Plan breaks on purpose.

tip_think_aloud.short: In technical interviews, think out loud. Interviewers grade your reasoning, not just the answer.
tip_think_aloud.more: If you're stuck, say what you'd try first and why.

tip_clarify_first.short: Ask clarifying questions before designing: users, scale, constraints.
tip_clarify_first.more: Jumping straight to a solution is a common junior mistake. Interviewers like the questions.

tip_star_stories.short: Prepare 5 stories as Situation, Task, Action, Result: conflict, failure, teamwork, a win, learning fast.
tip_star_stories.more: End each one with what you learned. The same stories answer many questions.

tip_teamwork_without_job.short: No team yet? Public coding projects, coding contests and freelance clients give you feedback and team stories.
tip_teamwork_without_job.more: Feedback on your code from strangers is a fast way to learn how teams work.

tip_ask_questions.short: Always ask a question at the end: what success looks like in 90 days, how the team works, real hours.
tip_ask_questions.more: It shows interest, and the answers tell you whether you want the job.

tip_fundamentals.short: Frameworks change fast. Fundamentals transfer: data structures, databases, networking, testing.
tip_fundamentals.more: Learn one stack well, but keep the basics sharp. They show up in every interview.

tip_ai_tools.short: Use AI tools where allowed, but understand and test every line. You'll be asked to explain it.
tip_ai_tools.more: Say what you used and how you checked it.

tip_secrets.short: A leaked password is no longer secret. Report it so it gets changed; deleting the message isn't enough.
tip_secrets.more: Never paste passwords into chats, emails or code.

tip_small_changes.short: Release small, tested updates early in the week. Friday releases are how weekends die.
tip_small_changes.more: Small updates are easier to check and easier to undo.

tip_give_credit.short: Credit teammates publicly. It builds trust, and people remember who shares.
tip_give_credit.more: It also makes your own wins more believable.

tip_blameless.short: Good teams review mistakes without blame: what happened, how it was fixed, and what stops a repeat.
tip_blameless.more: Owning your part calmly is a strength, not a confession.

tip_privacy.short: Customer data is off-limits without a business reason. Access is logged.
tip_privacy.more: Snooping is a fast way to lose a job and to hurt real people.

tip_focus_time.short: Protect focus time: decline meetings you aren't needed in and ask for notes.
tip_focus_time.more: Say what you're working on and when you'll be free.

tip_scope.short: When a deadline is impossible, offer a smaller first version and write down the risks.
tip_scope.more: Flag slips early. Surprises are worse than bad news.

tip_negotiate.short: A polite counter with a number and a reason is normal. It rarely backfires.
tip_negotiate.more: Know your market rate first. The usual worst case is 'this is our best offer'. Tight deadline? Asking for a few more days is normal.

tip_total_comp.short: Compare total pay: salary, bonus, equity, benefits and commute. 3 hours a day on a bus is a pay cut.
tip_total_comp.more: Ask about office days, on-call and real working hours too. Tight deadline? Asking for a few more days is normal.

tip_equity_lottery.short: Treat startup equity like a lottery ticket. Ask the percentage and the vesting schedule.
tip_equity_lottery.more: A 1-year cliff means you get nothing if you leave or are laid off before 12 months. Also ask the strike price and how long you'd have to buy vested options after leaving.

tip_fine_print.short: Read non-compete, IP and probation clauses. Enforceability varies by country and state. Unsure? Ask a lawyer.
tip_fine_print.more: Ask HR what a clause covers and get the answer in writing before you sign. Whether it's enforceable is a question for an employment lawyer or legal aid.

tip_written_offer.short: Don't stop other applications until you have a signed, written offer.
tip_written_offer.more: Check that it lists the start date, pay and work mode.
